name: Perhexiline

own_problems.text: Pulled from the market in United Kingdom and Spain, first in 1985 — for liver harm and nerve and brain harm

examples.title: Open-Label Study of Perhexiline in Patients With Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy and Moderate to Severe Heart Failure

summary: Perhexiline was removed from the market in the United Kingdom and Spain starting in 1985 due to liver damage and neurotoxicity, which is harm to the nervous system [3]. In a study testing the drug for heart failure, the trial ended early because the medication was not effective [5]. In addition, a small computer model rather than testing on people estimated low risk scores of 36 for the liver and 34 for the heart [M].
